findings.title: Shared error variable races in index build errgroup
findings.body: In searchSupport.init every goroutine in the errgroup assigns to the same outer err variable with `_, _, err = s.build(...)` and increments totalBatchesIndexed without synchronization. Concurrent builds race: one goroutine can overwrite another goroutine's error with nil before it is returned, so errgroup.Wait can report success even though an index failed to build. The batch counter is also unreliable. Use a local err inside each goroutine and protect the counter.

findings.title: Removing the full BuildIndex lock leaves same-key builds unprotected
findings.body: BuildIndex now only takes cacheMu around the final map write. getOrCreateIndex still performs an unsynchronized check-then-build, so two concurrent searches or watch events for the same NamespacedResource can both enter BuildIndex. For file-backed indexes both calls can try to create/open the same Bleve directory, and for all indexes the later cache write can overwrite an index that has already received events, leaving the cache pointing at a stale snapshot. A per-key singleflight or build lock is needed, not just locking the map write.

findings.title: TotalDocs iterates the cache without the cache lock
findings.body: bleveBackend.TotalDocs ranges over b.cache without taking cacheMu. The new log call `s.log.Info(..., s.search.TotalDocs())` in searchSupport.init runs immediately after the watch goroutine is started, and that goroutine can call getOrCreateIndex -> BuildIndex and write b.cache[key] under cacheMu. Concurrent map iteration and map write can panic or race. TotalDocs should take cacheMu.RLock, or the cache access should be restructured.

findings.title: Search event watcher panics on closed event channel during shutdown
findings.body: The watcher started in searchSupport.init uses context.Background() and never checks whether the events channel was closed. On server.Stop the SQL backend cancels its poller and closes the events channel; this loop then receives nil and calls handleEvent(nil), which dereferences evt.Type and panics. Because this PR now initializes search at startup, this watcher is always running. Use the server's cancellable context and handle the channel-close case by returning.

findings.title: Constructor leaks startup resources when Init fails
findings.body: NewResourceServer now calls s.Init(ctx) before returning, but on failure it returns nil without calling s.cancel() or s.lifecycle.Stop(). By that point searchSupport.init may already have started its background watcher, and lifecycle.Init may have acquired database or other resources. Since the caller receives nil, it cannot call Stop, so those resources and goroutines leak. The constructor should clean up/cancel on initialization failure.

findings.title: Postgres storage-server startup coverage is skipped
findings.body: The integration test now skips Postgres entirely. This is the test that exercises storage-server startup, which is exactly the behavior changed by moving unified-storage initialization into NewResourceServer. Without a replacement test, a Postgres startup regression, including failure of the eager index build, will not be caught. The test or environment should be fixed instead of skipping the backend.
